definitions.gloss: raindrops falling from eaves or rooftops; dripping rain
definitions.explanation: Water dripping from the edge of a roof or eaves during or after rain. Can also refer to the sound or traces left by such dripping. Written as 雨垂れ in full kanji. A word with poetic and seasonal associations.

examples.japanese: ⟦{軒先|のきさき}→軒先：08402_nokisaki⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{雨|あま}だれ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ちている→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧。
examples.english: Raindrops are dripping from the eaves.

examples.japanese: {雨|あま}だれ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}き→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{眠|ねむ}り→眠り：13673_nemuri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ついた。
examples.english: I fell asleep listening to the sound of dripping rain.

examples.japanese: {雨|あま}だれ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{穿|うが}つ、⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{諺|ことわざ}→諺：02765_kotowaza⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a proverb that says 'raindrops wear through stone.'

notes:
USAGE:
{雨|あま}だれ has a gentle, atmospheric quality and often appears in literary descriptions of rainy days. The proverb {雨|あま}だれ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{穿|うが}つ (raindrops wear through stone) is the Japanese equivalent of 'constant dripping wears away the stone,' meaning persistence overcomes any obstacle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雨|あま}だれ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧ (the sound of dripping rain)
- {雨|あま}だれ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧ (raindrops fall/drip)
- {雨|あま}だれ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{穿|うが}つ (constant effort brings results — proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{雨粒|あまつぶ}→雨粒：20328_amatsubu⟧ (raindrop) refers to individual drops of rain falling from the sky, while {雨|あま}だれ specifically means water dripping from eaves or a roof edge.
